definitionReview.actualCategory: The product remains identifiable physical tea leaves after steaming, rolling, hot-air drying and finishing. Article1 expressly covers dead plants/parts; the Arabic original confirms that wording. This is a stronger textual dead-material inclusion than TC's plant-parts definition without a living qualification. It does not mean every chemically derived plant ingredient is necessarily a plant part.
definitionReview.affirmativeDuty: Article1 agricultural consignment includes plants, plant products, or other regulated materials. Article5(2) then imposes certification on every imported/transit agricultural consignment. The final qualification concerning other regulated materials does not textually convert the separately enumerated plants limb into a future-designated-only category. Article3 limits application to cases specified by the Law and its executive regulations; Article5 is itself such an operative case. Article1's reference to a single certificate where appropriate describes consignment documentation and does not cancel the express all-consignment duty.
definitionReview.strongestContrary: Article1 definitions apply unless context requires otherwise. The more specific manufactured-product limb regulates manufactured materials only when their nature/processing can introduce/spread pests. MAFF-described sencha manufacture plus ISPM32 Category1 tea is strong factual evidence of sufficient processing. Reading finished tea exclusively in that product limb avoids overlapping definitions and fits Article2 pest-prevention purpose and Article4(1)(i)/(o) standards-related duties. This is a plausible favorable reading, not dismissed simply because tea is unnamed. It nevertheless requires the independent explicit dead-plant-part limb to yield; no provision in the full Act states that allocation. The conservative proposal retains the express dead-parts wording rather than claiming technical pest risk proved.
definitionReview.designationCheck: Article4 gives regulatory powers and Article14 permits further prohibitions/restrictions. Those powers are not the source of the proposed certificate duty; Article5(2) already supplies it directly for the defined consignment. Do not infer duty from mere enabling powers or customs tax-table absence.
definitionReview.exceptions: Article5(5)(c) is an administrative power to cancel prescribed conditions based on risk within the listed Ministry measures; it does not state a self-executing manufactured-food exemption. Article27(2) preserves older regulations only so far as compatible. The saved JKI partial German translation of Decision248/2003 Article2 uses living plants, but cannot narrow the newer Act's express live/dead definition. Its Article15(5) personal exception concerns traveler permits and Article25 small-quantity certificate exception concerns carried fruit/cut flowers/bulbs/tubers; neither establishes an automatic Japan postal-tea waiver. That partial translation is supplementary, not proof of absence of every possible older rule.
definitionReview.japanGuidance: Fresh original MAFF PDF page1 is dated21April2026 and has UAE Q*11 in the manufactured-green-tea column. Q means export with phytosanitary certificate; *11 warns some items may fall outside quarantine with neither permit nor certificate. JETRO August2025 separately states processed dried tea/matcha may be exempt subject to UAE confirmation; it predates the new Act. These are qualified corroboration, not an unconditional national duty or waiver.
definitionReview.privateFood: Existing personal-food registration exemption and unaccompanied-personal-food guidance are preserved. Their quantity/category gaps are not used as an independent certificate barrier. No commercial food documentation list is imported into private-post scope.

AE additionally says dead expressly. TC uses prior permit sections34–35; AE uses Article5(2) certificate. This supplies a substantive consistent distinction from BH/MV/KN/VC living-plant-plus-risk-manufacture regimes.

This independent food-certificate duty prevents a no-certificate route under the broad scope of the enacted rule.

Applying that food-certificate rule to a paid 100 g sealed tea parcel for personal consumption is a stated legal-scope inference; personal postal tea is not separately named in that decision. permitFreeReason: The actual enacted Decision 101/1 Article 1 requires an appropriate listed food certificate with every imported consignment, while Article 2 expressly covers packaged tea. The decision contains no personal-use or small-quantity exception. Applying its unqualified wording to a paid personal postal tea order is an explicit legal-scope inference. Decision 208/1 of 4 May 2009 changes only Article 2’s first paragraph on laboratory testing, leaving Article 1 intact; Decision 349/1 of 8 August 2022 regulates laboratory-result validity/retesting without waiving food certificates. The store cannot satisfy this independent requirement without certificates. This is not a finding that tea is prohibited, nor a resolution of manufactured tea’s separate phytosanitary classification. LibanPost’s unspecified preapproval threshold does not establish a certificate exemption.

rule: Iraq Agricultural Quarantine Law 76/2012, consolidated by the Ministry of Justice with the 2020 amendment, Article 1(4) covers plant-origin products prepared without diverting them from their plant nature. The original Arabic gazette uses طبيعتها النباتية. Factory sencha remains dried plant leaves after steaming and drying, so coverage is a reasonable conservative legal-scope inference. Article 7(1) requires an import licence for covered plant-product consignments. Article 9(1) expressly waives the phytosanitary certificate for qualifying non-agricultural consignments received by post up to 10 kg; Article 9(2) separately waives the import licence only for specified seed-registration samples. The described tea parcel is therefore unsuitable for the store’s no-permit route under this reading, rather than prohibited tea.
personalMailApplicability: Post offices are expressly included in Article 1(18); Article 9(1) expressly addresses mail as well as travellers and shipped consignments. The certificate-only waiver can plausibly cover this 100 g personal beverage parcel, but the separate import licence remains under the conservative plant-nature reading.

quantityLimit.scope: Article 9(1) certificate exemption only for qualifying non-agricultural-purpose consignments; not an import-licence waiver or permission to ship.
quantityLimit.weightBasisCaveat: Law says weight of materials, without expressly defining net or gross.

permitFreeReason: Conservative exclusion based on the domestic plant-nature definition plus the explicit distinction between the postal certificate waiver and the seed-only licence waiver. contraryInterpretation: Factory manufacturing could be regarded as diverting tea from plant nature. Unlike an explicit pest-risk-qualified manufactured-products definition, this requires interpreting a different statutory phrase; pest freedom alone does not establish the exclusion. No published current tea exemption or general postal licence waiver was found.
decisionReviewTrigger: No additional fact is needed to apply the conservative no-permit exclusion. A current published exclusion of manufactured tea from plant products or a separate applicable postal import-licence waiver would reverse it. The strongest contrary interpretation is that steaming/rolling/drying sufficiently transforms plant nature; the recovered law does not define the threshold or specifically classify sencha. This uncertainty is recorded rather than presented as an official tea determination.
